QuadriFlow — vendored source
============================

Upstream:  https://github.com/hjwdzh/QuadriFlow
Commit:    27a6867
License:   MIT — see LICENSE.txt
Paper:     Huang, Zhou, Niessner, Shewchuk, Guibas,
           "QuadriFlow: A Scalable and Robust Method for Quadrangulation",
           SGP 2018

Taken from **Blender's** arrangement of it (`extern/quadriflow`), not from
upstream directly, and `patches/blender.patch` is theirs, recorded here for
provenance. Blender is what makes this buildable outside its authors' machine:
it replaces the Boost dependency with a single bundled max-flow header
(`patches/boykov_kolmogorov_max_flow.hpp`) and bundles lemon under `3rd/`.

On top of that, **this project's own patch** is `review.patch`.

What is vendored
----------------
`src/` holds exactly the translation units Blender's `CMakeLists.txt` compiles,
plus the headers they include. Not vendored: `main.cpp` (the command line, which
wants Boost.ProgramOptions), `Optimizer.cu` (CUDA), `post-solver.cpp` (Ceres)
and `dedge.cpp`'s `serialize` path's dependencies. Nothing here reaches any of
them.

`3rd/lemon-1.3.1/` is lemon, trimmed to `lemon/` plus its LICENSE and AUTHORS —
the documentation, tests, demos and build system are not headers the compiler
would reach. Its `lemon/config.h` is normally produced by CMake's
`configure_file`; this build has no such step, so the file is **generated once
and committed**, and its own header says what the answers are and why.

`3rd/pcg32/` is the random number generator upstream pulls in as a submodule.

Notably absent: Intel TBB. Every parallel path in this tree is behind
`WITH_TBB`, which Blender never defines and neither does this build (one
translation unit even force-`#undef`s it). So what is compiled here is entirely
**serial** — which costs some speed on a large object and buys reproducibility
for free, unlike `third_party/instant-meshes`, which needed a TBB shim and a
determinism contract to get the same guarantee.

The patch
---------
P1  `src/optimizer.cpp` — three `solver.factorize(A)` calls gain a check that
    it worked.

    `EIGEN_MPL2_ONLY` (which this build defines, so the licence of what ships
    stays MPL-2.0) makes upstream select `Eigen::SparseLU` in place of
    `SimplicialLLT`. `SparseLU` reports a failed factorization through `info()`
    and leaves its internal supernodal matrix unallocated; upstream never
    checks, and the `solve()` on the next line then reads through a null
    pointer. That is a **segfault**, not a bad answer, and it is reachable from
    a real game asset — `assets/test_models/SM_Ammo_Crate_01a.fbx` reproduced it
    before this patch.

    The check throws, `src/remesh_quadriflow.cpp` catches, and
    `crates/optimize/src/remesh/` falls back to the field-based extraction,
    which has no comparable failure mode. The user gets a mesh and a warning
    naming the stage that gave up.

Refreshing this directory is: copy Blender's newer `extern/quadriflow` in,
update the commit above, re-apply `review.patch` (`git apply
third_party/quadriflow/review.patch`), regenerate the patch from the result,
re-generate `lemon/config.h` if upstream's `config.h.in` changed, and re-run
`crates/optimize`'s `remesh` suite — which includes a test that an asset the
solver cannot lay out comes back as a warning and a mesh rather than as a crash.

How it is built
---------------
`crates/optimize/build.rs`'s `build_quadriflow` compiles this alongside
`src/remesh_quadriflow.cpp`, gated on this directory (and on
`third_party/instant-meshes` + `third_party/eigen`, which it shares), setting
`cfg(has_quadriflow)`. Delete it and the workspace still builds: the "Only
quads" topology stays in the menu — so a preset naming it does not silently mean
something else — and falls back to "Mostly quads" with a warning.

It is a **separate translation unit** from the Instant Meshes bridge on purpose:
that tree's `common.h` defines `Vector3f`, `MatrixXu` and friends at global
scope, and this one brings Eigen's own names in for `namespace qflow`. Including
both in one file is a collision waiting to happen.
